subject: general
question:
According to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), India’s

 Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends upto __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**200 nautical miles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends up to **200 nautical miles** from the baseline as per the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).**
 
• The EEZ allows a coastal nation to exercise **sovereign rights** over natural resources, including energy production from water and wind, within this zone.
 
• UNCLOS, adopted in **1982**, defines the rights and responsibilities of nations regarding their use of the world's oceans.
 
• Within the EEZ, India has exclusive rights to exploit and manage **marine resources, fisheries, and mineral exploration.**
 
• UNCLOS ensures that nations respect each other's EEZ boundaries to maintain international peace and cooperation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baseline:** The baseline is the low-water line along the coast, from which the 200 nautical miles for the EEZ is measured.
 
• **Territorial Sea:** It extends up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline, where the coastal nation exercises complete sovereignty.
 
• **Contiguous Zone:** It extends from 12 to 24 nautical miles, where a country can enforce laws related to customs, immigration, and pollution.
 
• **High Seas:** Beyond the EEZ lies the high seas, which are international waters not under the jurisdiction of any country.
 
• **UNCLOS Significance:** UNCLOS provides a framework for resolving disputes and ensures equitable sharing of marine resources among nations.
